coupling_edges.limits: Design-only: the written-layer-plus-register-reading coupling is a declared rule of a fictional language, not a claim about how Hittite or Hattic scribal practice worked, and no real-language genealogy is asserted. S01 is partial-support, mediated English teaching prose with tertiary corroborations; no cuneiform autograph or Hattic-language text was read; the Hattic non-IE and no-established-Caucasian-genealogy legs stay unsupported and the source stays partial.
coupling_edges.mechanism: S01's retrieved lesson gloss marks a written Akkadogram (IS-BAT, romanized) whose explicitly stated Hittite reading differs (epta): one written citation form with a distinct spoken realization, declared inside a single clause. D3 copies only that separation as a constructed rule: U01/U02 both write lexeme L01's E0 citation spelling pina as written_form, while the market-ordinary reading (U01) uses the SC1-changed E1 spoken form and the hall-ritual reading (U02) is governed by the exactly matching avoidance rule AV1, which substitutes L02's E0 form. Written form and spoken form are therefore separable, declared slots rather than one identical string.

coupling_edges.applicability: design-only; eras and audiences as recorded on the target records
coupling_edges.limits: Design-only construction on a fictional felt work garment; no real textile history is claimed and no statement is made about pleats, linen or felt in any real tradition. S02 is scoped-support from a museum object record carrying the museum's own dating caveat; findspot dating is catalogue attribution, not independent re-dating; record fields are transcriptions, not running prose; no cutting or pleating-set reconstruction exists here.
coupling_edges.mechanism: S02's museum record dates a pleated linen tunic to late Dynasty 11-early Dynasty 12, a garment feature attested before the period it is sometimes used to date, showing that one object-level trait cannot serve as an exclusive era marker. D3 transfers that caution: C01 (E0) and C02 (E1) keep the same M01 felt work-garment silhouette, so the two fictional eras are not distinguishable by a single decorative feature, and era assignment rides on declared material availability routes rather than on object appearance. No garment cut is reconstructed for either costume.

S03 is translation-mediated English (Oldenberg 1892, including at least one conjectural emendation); the Sanskrit was not read; it is one school's domestic-rule text.
